lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: washing hands all the way

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 3 — kitchen helper safety and no-heat preparation
objective: Learners demonstrate and self-check a complete five-step handwashing sequence (wet hands, apply soap, scrub every surface including between fingers and under nails for twenty seconds, rinse until soap is gone, dry with a clean towel) at a real sink, then compare their own starting habits against the full sequence to identify which steps they already do and which steps they normally skip.
scenario: At a bathroom or kitchen sink, before any new instruction, the learner washes their hands the way they normally would while a family member watches quietly without coaching, so both can see the learner's starting habits. The learner then learns the full five-step sequence and washes again, timing the twenty-second scrub by singing the alphabet song once through.
safetyNotes: Use only a sink, soap, and a towel for this lesson; ask a trusted adult before touching anything else in the kitchen.

tasks.directions: Before learning the five-step sequence, wash your hands the way you normally do, without any new instructions.

prompts.text: List each thing you did, in order, when you washed your hands just now.

tasks.directions: Now learn and practice the full five-step sequence at the sink: wet your hands, add soap, scrub every surface for twenty seconds (backs of hands, between fingers, under nails), rinse until the soap is gone, and dry with a clean towel.

prompts.text: I wet my hands with running water before adding soap.
I scrubbed the backs of my hands, between my fingers, and under my nails, not just my palms.
I scrubbed for the full twenty seconds, timed by singing the alphabet song once through.
I dried my hands completely with a clean towel before touching anything else.

tasks.directions: Later today, without looking back at this sheet, wash your hands again from memory before you plan to touch any food.

prompts.text: Write the five steps in order from memory. Circle the step you almost forgot.

tasks.directions: Compare your baseline wash from task one to your full five-step wash.

prompts.text: Name one specific step you skipped in your very first wash today that you now do every time, and explain why that step matters.

remediation: If a learner rinses off the soap in under ten seconds because scrubbing without a timer feels long enough, reteach by having them scrub through one full round of the alphabet song sung out loud before rinsing, so they feel the actual twenty-second length instead of guessing at it.
extension: Have the learner teach the five-step sequence to a stuffed animal or another household member willing to listen, narrating each step out loud in order, to test whether they can explain the sequence and not just perform it themselves.
